decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'In the box at the top, paste this link and press Save' — saving a bookmark by url works; round 3 client: 'this behaves the way I hoped'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url conforms to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'it should fill itself in on its own — a title, a short description, the site's little icon, a preview image'; round 3 client: 'That set of details feels sufficient.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Auto-collection of title/description/favicon/preview matches REF-BM-02 (site name extra but non-divergent). Conforming.

decisions.evidence: round 4 maker: 'Change the title... Adjust the description text too'; round 4 client: 'title plus description is the right boundary for correcting automatically gathered details'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing auto-collected title/description before/after saving conforms to REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: round 4 maker: 'I made only the title and description editable... leaving the preview image, icon, and site name as automatically gathered. Is that the right boundary?'; round 4 client: 'Later, when managing the full bookmark, I'll also want to edit its URL, tags, and note'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented edit scope (title/description only) omits reference-required editing of url, tags, note. Client requests the missing reference requirements -> extend. Delivered later (round 11 url).

decisions.evidence: round 5 maker: 'In the Tags field, type testing and press Enter — it becomes a little chip'; round 5 client: 'The overall organizing behavior matches what I had in mind.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one/more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: round 5 maker: 'The note is a free-text private area shown on the card. Is that what you pictured a note being?'; round 5 client: 'The note should be private and support simple Markdown formatting when displayed.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented note was plain free-text (no markdown), diverging from REF-BM-23 (markdown note rendered when viewing). Client supplies the reference-conforming markdown behaviour -> correct.

decisions.evidence: round 5 maker offers three tag-entry styles side by side ('tag-entry-compare.html ... only the tag-entry method differs'); round 5 client: 'I prefer C — Pick or type, because I can quickly reuse existing tags while still creating a new one when needed.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-10 (offer existing tags on entry); client selects the conforming 'pick or type' option -> select. Offered decision marked diverged=true.

decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'title, the description, and site name stacked to the right' plus favicon; round 7 list shows tags/filters; round 7 client: 'The basic finding flow feels right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title, description, favicon and (via tags added round 5) tags conforms to REF-BM-07; layout composition is orthogonal UI.

decisions.evidence: round 7 maker: 'Click the reference tag chip in the filter row. The list narrows to bookmarks carrying that tag'; round 7 client: 'The basic finding flow feels right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Filtering to a specific tag conforms to REF-BM-11. Multi-tag AND semantics discussed are orthogonal to reference (not specified).

decisions.evidence: round 7 maker: 'I made it match against the title, description, tags, note, and site name all at once' (URL omitted); round 7 client: 'I want it to... cover the title, description, note, and URL.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented search scope omitted URL, diverging from REF-BM-12 (title/description/note/url). Client supplies the reference-conforming scope adding URL -> correct.

decisions.evidence: round 7 maker presents search without stating case behaviour; round 7 client: 'I want it to be case-insensitive'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitivity (REF-BM-13) missing from presented/asked scope; client requests the reference requirement -> extend. Implemented round 8.

decisions.evidence: round 7 maker presents plain substring search; round 7 client: 'I'd also like #tag searches'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag syntax (REF-BM-14) absent from presented scope; client requests it -> extend. Implemented round 8.

decisions.evidence: round 7 client: 'more precise searches using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses'; round 8 maker confirms operators/parentheses resolve.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean operators + parentheses (REF-BM-15) absent from presented scope; client requests them -> extend.

decisions.evidence: round 7 client: 'quoted exact phrases'; round 8 maker demos '"test suite"' exact phrase.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Quoted exact-phrase matching (REF-BM-16) absent from presented scope; client requests it -> extend.

decisions.evidence: round 9 maker: 'I made Read later an additional marker... The alternative would be to move it out of All so it only shows under Read Later'; round 9 client: 'I think of Read Later as an additional marker, so the bookmark should remain in All while also appearing in the separate list.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered marker-vs-move alternatives differ in fulfilment: reference models unread as a flag (bookmark stays in collection, REF-BM-17/18); client selects the conforming marker option -> select. Offered decision diverged=true.

decisions.evidence: round 9 maker demos marking and viewing read-later but not un-marking; round 9 client: 'Removing that marker once I've read it should take it out of Read Later without deleting the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read removal from unread list (REF-BM-19) missing from presented scope; client requests it -> extend.

decisions.evidence: round 10 maker: 'kept safe with an Archived badge — nothing was deleted... click Restore to library'; round 10 client: 'remain safely available in Archive until restored'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive-as-reversible (restore) conforms to REF-BM-27's reversibility. (Actual delete never demonstrated — see REF-BM-05.)

decisions.evidence: round 10 maker: 'You now have a third tab, Archive... There's your archived bookmark'; round 10 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Separate archived-list view conforms to REF-BM-28.

decisions.evidence: round 10 maker: archiving 'moves a bookmark out of All (and out of Read Later)' — search exclusion not stated; round 10 client: 'it should disappear from the main library, Read Later, and ordinary searches, but remain safely available in Archive'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented archive behaviour omitted exclusion from ordinary search (part of REF-BM-26 and edge-case rule); client requests the search-exclusion requirement -> extend.

decisions.evidence: round 11 maker: 'You'll now see the Link (URL) at the top of the form'; round 11 client: 'This editing flow works for me.'
decisions.note: Implementation review of the url-editing requirement the client extended in round 4; now presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: round 13 maker: 'Does that match what you'd want... no duplicate, just take me to the existing one? Or would you rather it let you save a second copy anyway?'; round 13 client: 'don't create a duplicate. Taking me to and highlighting the existing bookmark, where I can edit it if needed'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives (dedupe-to-existing vs allow second copy) differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-06; client selects the conforming dedupe-and-edit-existing option -> select. Offered decision diverged=true.

decisions.evidence: round 17 maker presents 'everything that's settled... 12 flows' as the complete first version (no delete flow); round 17 client: 'Yes, please start implementing this scope. It covers the first version I want.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Deleting a bookmark (REF-BM-05) is never presented; archive-vs-delete was only alluded to (round 10). Completeness scope omits it; client approves without expressing the difference -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: round 17 maker completeness summary and round 18 acceptance list contain no 'click item opens original url' behaviour; round 17 client approves scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Selecting a list item to navigate to the original url (REF-BM-08) never surfaced; approved without expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: round 17 maker: complete '12 flows' summary contains no multi-select/bulk actions; round 17 client: 'It covers the first version I want.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk actions over multiple selected bookmarks (REF-BM-20) omitted from the declared-complete scope; approved without expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: round 17 completeness summary contains no 'apply to whole filtered collection' action; round 17 client approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk action across the whole current-filter collection (REF-BM-21) never surfaced; approved without expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: round 17 completeness summary has no sort-key control; round 17 client: 'It covers the first version I want.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sorting the list by a sort key (REF-BM-22) never presented; approved without expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: round 17 completeness summary contains no local HTML/PDF snapshot; round 17 client approves scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local single-file HTML snapshot (with PDF rule) (REF-BM-24) never surfaced; approved without expression -> unexpressed (extended item).

decisions.evidence: round 17 completeness summary contains no Internet Archive snapshot; round 17 client approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Internet Archive snapshot creation (REF-BM-25) never surfaced; approved without expression -> unexpressed (extended item).

decisions.note: Specification gate. Saving a search+tags combination as a reusable bundle (REF-BM-29) never surfaced; approved without expression -> unexpressed (extended item).
